resources.string: Either the off switch is on or the fix hasn\'t started yet. The correction log shows which.
Fix is ON (root mode, not installed)
Root mode starts by itself after a restart, once root is on.
The installer only works on the Sonim XP3800 with Android 8.1.\n\nThis phone: Android %1$s, XP3800 keypad %2$s.

Installing needs root, but only for the install. The fix runs without root afterwards.\n\nGet root first (for example with Root Manager), then come back. Or install from a computer: see the README on GitHub.
Undo needs root. Without root you can still turn the fix off (Turn off / on), or flash your system backup over EDL.
The fix is already installed. To reinstall, use Undo, restart the phone, then install again.

Check install reruns the install\'s final checks with root, changing nothing: the stock policy backup (.bak) is the stock policy with its stock label, and /system holds what was installed. Use it after an install that showed \"failed\" after \"Installed. Reboot to start it.\"

Before you start, have a backup of the system partition and an EDL flashing setup, in case the phone won't boot.

The app will:
• Back up the stock policy on the phone, as .bak files next to the originals in /system/etc/selinux. Undo restores from them. (Untested: this backup has never been run on a phone. Keep your own copy too.)
• Compile the new policy the way the phone does at boot, and stop without changing anything if that fails.
• Install the daemon and the policy.

Afterwards, before you restart: remove root, or disable apps that ask for root at startup (such as Lucky Patcher). With the fix installed, getting root crashed the phone on almost every attempt.
The fix isn\'t installed, so there\'s nothing to undo.

This restores the stock policy from the .bak backup in /system/etc/selinux made when the fix was installed (older installs: from policy-backup/ copied to /data/local/tmp/kd_dry/stock), removes the daemon, and then asks you to restart.\n\nWarning: with the fix installed, getting root crashed the phone on almost every attempt during testing. If the phone restarts, try again. If it keeps failing, flash your system backup over EDL.
Turn the fix off or on

From a computer (no root needed):

Off:
adb shell touch /data/local/tmp/keydebounce.off
adb reboot

On:
adb shell rm /data/local/tmp/keydebounce.off
adb reboot

When the fix is off, the keypad works as it did before.
The fix isn\'t installed. If you run it in root mode, use Run with root (no install) → Stop, and turn off Start at boot.
With root, the app can do this now, without a restart. With the fix installed, getting root crashed the phone on almost every attempt during testing.

Starts the filter through root, the way Shizuku starts its server. Nothing in /system or the SELinux policy changes, and it stops when the phone restarts.

Start at boot is %1$s. When it's on, the filter starts by itself after a restart, once root is on.

The root has to allow access to the keypad and /dev/uinput (Magisk does). If it doesn't, the output shows why.
The fix is installed, so it already starts at boot. Root mode is for phones without the install.
Root mode needs root. Without root, the only option is the permanent install from a computer (see the README on GitHub).

No root needed. Tested: it fixes contact bounce (5 -> "55"). It cannot fix key overlap (5,6 -> "566"), which is the main problem and still needs the root daemon.

It can't be turned on from inside the app. From a computer, run the command in the README (Bounce filter section). It adds this service to the phone's accessibility list and keeps the others, such as Mouse Toggle. Don't replace the whole list with just this service.

Then restart the phone: on this phone, turning an accessibility service on or off only takes effect after a restart.

After reinstalling or updating this app, add it again and restart.

To turn it off: Settings ▸ Accessibility ▸ %2$s, or open Settings from here. Then restart.

(%1$s/.BounceFilterService)

No-root fallback that only fixes contact bounce (a key registering twice from one press). It does not fix key overlap (two keys pressed close together); that still needs the root daemon. See the README on GitHub.
Start at boot is %1$s.\n\nWhen it\'s on, the filter starts by itself after a restart, with nothing to tap. With a root that\'s on at boot (Magisk) it starts right away.

With Root Manager, the first root request after each restart runs its kernel exploit, which can crash the phone. After a restart the app checks every 30 seconds; once su has been there on two checks in a row (about 30 seconds after the phone finishes starting), it starts root and the filter by itself. If that ever crashes the phone, the next restart asks first instead of trying again, so it can\'t turn into a reboot loop. If something else starts root sooner (for example su in Termux), the filter starts 30 to 60 seconds after that.

On the last restart, starting root and the filter never finished: Root Manager\'s exploit probably crashed the phone. So this time it asks instead of trying again.\n\nStart tries once more. Not now leaves it off; the next restart tries automatically again.
Start at boot is on. It takes effect after a restart.

Nothing has used root since the phone restarted. Root Manager\'s su is always installed, but the first root request after each restart runs its kernel exploit. That takes about a second and can crash and restart the phone. After that, root requests are instant and safe until the next restart.\n\nStart root now? Or start it another way first (su in Termux, or adb shell su), then try again.
With the fix installed, the exploit crashed the phone on almost every attempt during testing.
Start at boot is on. After a restart the filter starts by itself once root is on.
Couldn\'t restart (%s). Restart with the power key.
Granted. Press Close: the app closes so the permission takes effect. Then open it again.

The correction log needs permission to read the phone's log. Apps can't ask for it with a normal prompt, but with root this app can grant it to itself.

Without root, from a computer:
adb shell pm grant %1$s android.permission.READ_LOGS

You can also do this later from the Correction log screen.
Not run: root hasn\'t started since the restart, and starting it runs Root Manager\'s kernel exploit, which can crash the phone. Nothing was changed.
No result: root wasn\'t available, was refused, or stopped partway. If there\'s no output above, nothing was changed; otherwise the output shows how far it got.
It stopped at the step shown above. Everything before that step is listed in the output.
This screen was restarted, so the command wasn\'t run again. Check the status on the main screen.
Dry run passed. Nothing on the phone was changed.

Installed.

Before you restart: remove root, or disable apps that ask for root at startup (such as Lucky Patcher).

The stock policy is backed up as .bak files in /system/etc/selinux. Undo restores from them.

Then restart the phone to turn the fix on.

The install checks out: the stock policy backup (.bak) verifies, and /system holds what was installed.\n\nIf you haven\'t restarted since installing: disable apps that ask for root at startup (such as Lucky Patcher), or remove root, then restart to turn the fix on.
Removed. Restart the phone to finish.
Off. The keypad works unfiltered now, and the fix stays off after restarts until you turn it back on.
Running. It stops when the phone restarts, unless Start at boot is on.

Before restarting, remove root or disable apps that ask for root at startup (such as Lucky Patcher). With the fix installed, an app that asks for root at startup can cause a reboot loop.\n\nIf you\'re removing root first, restart with the power key afterwards.
Restart to finish removing the fix.
Type in the box. Every press is listed below, newest first. The extra digit comes from overlaps (a key pressed while another is held); with the fix on there should be none. Press Back to exit.

The app needs a one-time permission to read the log. With root, press Grant with root. Or from a computer:

adb shell pm grant %1$s android.permission.READ_LOGS
adb shell am force-stop %1$s

Then open the app again.
Counts cover what\'s still in the phone\'s log, usually since the last restart.
At its last start the off switch was on, so it exited.
No keydebounce lines in the log yet. Startup messages can get pushed out of the log during boot.
